name: run_status
description: The broadcast now, numbered by revision: every task with its state, live status, branch, last commit and a one-line summary, and what is open: questions waiting, prompts waiting on the user, tasks ready to accept, tasks possibly stalled, anything uncertain. A task with tabs added by open_tab lists every worker tab under tabs, its first worker as main, and is ready to accept only once every tab ended its turn; a prompt in an added tab is named task/tab, and a tab that was closed is marked closed and never opened again. Under run it also shows the off-brief finds, each agent's weekly use, and each installed agent's models with its default model. Call it first after any restart or compaction.

name: jira_search
description: Searches Jira, read-only, within the Jira projects linked to the broadcast's projects.

name: jira_create
description: Creates a Jira ticket in one of the broadcast's Jira projects. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and outside its Jira projects; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. The same key returns the ticket the first call made, so call again with it after a lost reply.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

project.description: The Jira project's key, one of the broadcast's.

type.description: The issue type, such as Task, Bug or Story.

description.description: What the ticket says, in plain text.

parent.description: The key of the epic or parent ticket it belongs under, if any.

name: jira_move
description: Moves a Jira ticket to the status of that name, by the transition that leads there. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and outside its Jira projects. A status the ticket cannot reach from where it is is refused with the statuses it can reach.

key.description: The ticket's key, such as PAY-231.

status.description: The status to move it to, such as In Review or Done.

name: jira_link
description: Links two Jira tickets, read from the first: the first blocks, relates to or duplicates the second. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and when either is outside its Jira projects.

key.description: The ticket the link is read from.

type.description: The Jira link type's name, such as Blocks, Relates or Duplicate.

name: create_task
description: Adds an unstarted task to the open plan revision, in one of the broadcast's projects. The same key in this broadcast returns the task already made. Once the first plan is submitted, additions past a quarter of its size need the Oracle's yes, which may answer pending: call again with its challengeId. One the Oracle refuses, or any past that limit with the Oracle off, is refused and noted for the summary by AiTerm.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

title.description: The task's title, as its row shows it.

brief.description: The worker's first prompt: everything it needs, since it sees nothing else.

project.description: The project it belongs to, one of the broadcast's, by name or by id from run_status.

ticket.description: The Jira key it works, if any.

agent.description: The agent that works the task, among those installed.

model.description: A model id from the agent's own list, as run_status shows it under agents. Left out, the agent's default. A model not in that list is refused.

modelReason.description: Why this agent and model, in one line, as the task's card and the summary show it.

agentPinned.description: True when the person's words named this task's agent: it then starts on that agent whatever its weekly use.

end.description: Where the task ends, from the broadcast's Done when: commit; draftMR, push and open a draft merge request; merge, push, open a merge request and merge it once the host says it can be; or mergeLocal, merge the accepted commit into the project's own default branch, with nothing pushed. A merge needs the broadcast's Merge slice. Left out, a task ends at a draftMR, or at a commit when the Done says a commit.

dependsOn.description: What the task waits for. An order dependency waits until the other task is accepted or needs no change; a code dependency also builds on its accepted commit, in the same project. At most one code dependency.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

challengeId.description: The challengeId a challenged call returned: send it with your revised arguments, or with challengeReply. A reply that says pending has no answer yet: call again with its challengeId and the same arguments. For create_task and finish_task, the call again acts only on the Oracle's yes. The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

challengeReply.description: Your answer to each point of the second opinion's critique, when you keep the act as it was.

name: update_task

A merge needs the broadcast's Merge slice. Left out, a task ends at a draftMR, or at a commit when the Done says a commit.

name: read_task
description: Reads a task: its worker's last message, its diff, the prompt open in its session, or its review: the agent review's findings, and for a task whose request people review, its threads with their ids, who approved and who was asked. A task with tabs added by open_tab: tab names the one whose last message or prompt to read. A key the task has no tab for is refused with its tabs.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

tab.description: For lastMessage and prompt, the key of the tab to read, as run_status lists it. Left out, or main, the first worker.

name: review_task
description: Starts an agent review of a working task's branch, before you accept it: another agent reads its commits, diff and worktree headless and read-only, as instructions asks, a skill they name passed to it as text. Nobody is notified, so it needs no slice. It answers started at once; AiTerm wakes you when the findings are in, and read_task with what: review reads them. Have the task's agent fix them with message_task. A review running already, or the same review of the same commit, is not started again.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

instructions.description: What the review checks and how, from the broadcast's Review, such as an adversarial review with /review-skill.

agent.description: Who reviews. Left out, the other of Claude and Codex from the task's own agent.

name: request_review
description: Marks a task's merge request ready and asks people to review it. Refused unless the broadcast's Review slice is on; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. The same reviewers again change nothing.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

reviewers.description: The usernames to ask, as find_user gives them.

name: reply_thread
description: Replies in a review thread on a task's merge request, by the thread's id from read_task with what: review. Refused unless the broadcast's Review slice is on. The same key posts once.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

name: find_user
description: Finds people on the code host of a task's project who may review there, by username or name. It only reads, so it needs no slice.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

query.description: A username or a name, or part of one.

name: message_task
description: Sends a started task's worker a message, typed into its session by AiTerm's rules. Returns delivered, partial (pasted, its Enter held back) or refused, with the reason; nothing is retried. A task with tabs added by open_tab: tab names the one to message. A key the task has no tab for is refused with its tabs.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

tab.description: The key of the tab to message, as run_status lists it. Left out, or main, the first worker.

name: open_tab
description: Adds a worker tab to a task that is working or in review: another agent in the task's window, on the same worktree and branch, for more work on that task. It is part of the task: one card, one branch, accepted once. Its first prompt is your brief, after AiTerm's lines on where it works and that it shares the worktree. It opens behind the user's work. The same key on the same task returns the first call's tab and opens nothing more; the same key with other arguments is refused. Returns the tab's key, agent, model, and opened or opening.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

agent.description: The agent that works the task, among those installed.

model.description: A model id from the agent's own list, as run_status shows it under agents. Left out, the agent's default. A model not in that list is refused.

modelReason.description: Why this agent and model, in one line.

agentPinned.description: True when the person's words named this agent: an agent whose workers can't be messaged is then not refused.

brief.description: The tab's first prompt: what this worker does, since it sees nothing else.

name: mark_task
description: Records a working task's outcome: accepted, with the result commit on its branch and the worker's check output; noChange; blocked or failed, with the reason in note. The same outcome for the same commit returns the earlier result.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

sha.description: The accepted commit, unmoved on the task's branch.

checkOutput.description: The worker's check output: tests, lint, build.

The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

name: resume_task
description: Puts a blocked task back to work once its reason is resolved; the same worker session continues.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

name: retry_task
description: Queues a failed task again, if it has retries left.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

name: finish_task
description: Carries out an accepted task's end from the plan, for its accepted commit only. draft MR: pushes the task's own branch and opens a draft merge request; a stacked task's targets its parent's branch, so finish the parent first. merge: pushes, opens a merge request and merges it at the accepted commit, once the host calls it mergeable with its pipelines green, read twice at least 30 seconds apart. A stacked task waits for its parent's merge, then retargets to the default branch. While it waits this answers waitingToMerge, and AiTerm wakes you when it merged or is blocked; after about an hour of waiting it answers blocked. A failed pipeline or a conflict blocks it: have the worker fix it, accept the new commit, and call finish_task again. A task that ends in a commit has nothing to finish. With the broadcast's Review written and its Review slice on, the request opens as a draft and the task goes into review instead, answering inReview: AiTerm wakes you on people's feedback, and the next finish_task after the last fix ends the review, a draft end published, a merge end going on to merge. A merge, through the request or local, is refused unless the broadcast's Merge slice is on; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. Before it merges a request that is still a draft, AiTerm marks it ready, only to merge it, and it merges only with every one of its review threads resolved. mergeLocal: merges the accepted commit into the project's own checkout's default branch and never pushes; that checkout must be on its default branch with nothing uncommitted. AiTerm leaves the push for the person, as "Push main in <project>: merged locally." With the Oracle on, a finish_task that would merge first needs the Oracle's yes that the conditions written in the Review and the Done hold; it may answer pending: call again with its challengeId. A no is recorded on the task and refuses the merge. It answers result: published, inReview, waitingToMerge, blocked, refused or failed, with reason, mergeRequest, pushedSHA, merged and mergedSHA as far as they are known; refused and failed also say what was already done. Each step is recorded and calling again resumes at the next step: it never pushes or opens a request twice, and on a task that is done it answers what was done. A push that timed out may have landed: call finish_task again. A takeover stops a merge's waiting: call finish_task again once the task is handed back. Refused if the task ends in a commit, the task was taken over, its branch moved past the accepted commit, its parent was accepted again, the broadcast is paused, stopped or offline, the host protects its branch or cannot say whether it does, or it is the default branch. AiTerm never deploys, never force-pushes, and never pushes to a default or protected branch.

name: ask_you
description: Asks the user a question: it shows under Waiting on you and notifies them. They answer in this window; close it with resolve_question. The same key returns the open question.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

question.description: The question, complete on its own.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

name: resolve_question
description: Closes a question the user answered, with a one-line summary of the answer.

name: report_find
description: Records something off-brief that you or an agent found, such as a leak in another module: it is not worked on, and the summary may mention it with why it matters. With the broadcast's Jira slice on, AiTerm also files it as a Task in the first of its Jira projects and answers the ticket's key, or why it could not. The same key is recorded once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

title.description: The find, in a few words.

why.description: Why it matters, in one line.

name: leave_for_you
description: Records what a slice kept you from doing, naming what is left and why. It changes no task and sends nothing. The same key is recorded once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

text.description: What is left for the person and why, in one sentence.

name: log_decision
description: Writes a decision you took on your own to the broadcast's log, for the summary. The same key is written once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

text.description: The decision, in a few words.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

why.description: Why you decided it, in one sentence.

objection.description: The Oracle's objection, when you decided against it.

name: write_summary
description: When the broadcast is complete, write its summary with write_summary: a few short paragraphs, in plain prose, no lists or headings. Say what was done and how it went, honestly: what went wrong and how it was handled, not only what succeeded. Fold in what you decided on your own and what you found along the way. Keep it short enough to read in a minute. Refused until the broadcast is complete; calling it again replaces the summary.

text.description: The summary: a few short paragraphs of plain prose.
